justifications.functional_suitability: Cataloging of physical and digital items (R-01) is explicitly supported by 'Catalog Management Service' alongside bulk imports. Circulation workflows and self-service portals are fully realized through 'Circulation Controller & Service' and 'Patron Web App & API'.
justifications.performance_efficiency: The sub-800ms search target (R-05) is addressed via a dedicated 'Search Engine' (OpenSearch), Kafka event-driven index synchronization, PgBouncer connection pooling, and token caching via Redis in 'Authentication & Authorization Filter Component'.
justifications.compatibility: Interoperability is thoroughly addressed with external systems: standard OIDC/OAuth 2.0 with 'External Identity Provider (IdP)', REST/TLS 1.3 for 'External Payment Gateway' and 'External Notification Service', and adapters for 'Interlibrary Loan (ILL) Network'.
justifications.usability: Patrons are served by 'Patron UI Component' using SSR/React for self-service, while staff use dedicated endpoints. However, dedicated UI interfaces for 'Librarians and Circulation Staff' and 'Library Administrators' are not explicitly defined at the container level.
justifications.reliability: Fault tolerance is reinforced via Resilience4j in 'Payment & ILL Client Adapters', asynchronous decoupling through Kafka, 'circulation.dlq' dead-letter queue handling, PgBouncer connection pooling, and automated OpenSearch snapshots.
justifications.security: EU data residency constraints are enforced across EU-hosted PostgreSQL, OpenSearch, and Kafka. Security is fortified with AES-256 encryption, TLS 1.3/mTLS, rate limiting, pgcrypto audit logging, and 'Data Masking Component' for patron PII protection.
justifications.maintainability: Decomposition follows clear domain boundaries across API Gateway, Staff Management API, Patron Web App & API, and Notification Dispatcher. Components exhibit high cohesion, decoupled asynchronous event publishing, and clean hexagonal-style client adapters.
justifications.portability: Services leverage widely supported runtime stacks (Go, Node.js, Spring Boot) and standard protocols. Relying on managed cloud dependencies (Kafka, OpenSearch, PostgreSQL) introduces slight vendor-specific coupling, though mitigated by open protocols.

PERF-01.justification: Managed OpenSearch cluster and Redis token caching at the API Gateway offload authentication overhead and provide sub-second search querying. However, explicit search result caching or autoscaling policies under peak load are not detailed.
sensitivity_points: OpenSearch cluster sizing and shard replication under high concurrent query loads
Redis token-cache hit ratio preventing latency degradation from the external IdP
tradeoffs: Memory footprint of Redis token caching versus latency reduction on request authorization

PERF-02.justification: Catalog updates are decoupled asynchronously via Kafka topics and processed by the Index Management Service using index aliasing, isolating write load from search queries and ensuring updates appear well within 5 minutes without query degradation.
sensitivity_points: Kafka consumer lag on catalog update events during sustained write throughput
tradeoffs: Eventual consistency of catalog updates versus near-instant search indexing performance

AVAIL-01.justification: The search engine utilizes an OpenSearch cluster with automated geo-redundant snapshots, allowing node failovers without complete outages. Circulation operations persist separately in PostgreSQL and remain fully operational even if search nodes fail.
sensitivity_points: Replica shard configuration in the OpenSearch cluster for transparent node failover
tradeoffs: Cost and storage overhead of maintaining replica shards versus failover recovery speed

AVAIL-02.justification: The API Gateway proxies stateless instances of the Patron Web App & API, routing traffic away from failed nodes. Transactional loan integrity is secured in PostgreSQL via connection pooling and ACID compliance.
sensitivity_points: API Gateway upstream health-check frequency and rapid traffic re-routing
tradeoffs: Aggressive health-check intervals increase network overhead to detect failed container instances

MOD-01.justification: Catalog Management Service handles digital and physical cataloging, but there is no specialized external e-book adapter abstraction. Adding a new provider requires modifying internal catalog service ingestion logic.
sensitivity_points: Coupling of external ingestion formats inside the monolithic Catalog Management Service
tradeoffs: Consolidated catalog service simplicity versus modular extensibility for varied external digital providers

MOD-02.justification: Circulation policies and loan rules reside directly in the Circulation Controller & Service. There is no external rule engine, configurable rule registry, or dynamic policy component to adjust rules without modifying and deploying code.
sensitivity_points: Hard-coded business logic in the circulation service requiring code redeployments
tradeoffs: Direct code logic execution performance versus flexibility of runtime dynamic configuration

SEC-01.justification: EU data residency is enforced by design across PostgreSQL, OpenSearch, Kafka, and external dispatch services. Outbound interlibrary cross-border flows pass through a dedicated Data Masking Component that strips or pseudonymizes patron PII.
sensitivity_points: Completeness of PII pseudonymization prior to external ILL cross-border egress
tradeoffs: Data processing overhead of inline PII masking versus absolute data sovereignty compliance

SEC-02.justification: Authentication and authorization filters validate tokens via external IdP, while Query Parser & Router applies Document-Level Security and RBAC. Audit logging streams to SIEM, though explicit loan-record ownership authorization checks in Patron API remain implicit.
sensitivity_points: Enforcement of user-resource ownership validation at the API controller layer
tradeoffs: Granular security audit logging on every read attempt versus SIEM ingestion overhead
